text:
git add -A src tests && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(spl): SplTempFileObject was a hand-rolled buffer, and it disagreed with php five ways

php's `SplTempFileObject` IS an `SplFileObject` on `php://temp`. elephc modelled it
with an in-memory buffer of its own — thirteen method bodies, a spill flag, a
position counter — and the two disagreed. MEASURED on `php -n` 8.5.6:

    $t = new SplTempFileObject();
    $t->eof()                          php: false   elephc: true
    …write "a\nbb\nccc\n", fseek(0)
    $t->current()                      php: "a\n"   elephc: "ccc"
    iterating it                       php keeps the newlines, elephc dropped them
    new SplTempFileObject(10)
    $t->getPathname()   php: php://temp/maxmemory:10   elephc: php://temp

Opening the stream php opens deletes all of it: 18 functions and four properties go
with it. The NAME keys off `ZEND_NUM_ARGS()` in php-src — no argument names
`php://temp`, an explicit one names `php://temp/maxmemory:N`, a negative one names
`php://memory` — and a synthesized body cannot count arguments, so the default value
stands in for "no argument". The two disagree only for an explicit
`new SplTempFileObject(2097152)`, which asks for the default in longhand.

The subclass still re-declares the parent's stream methods, with the parent's own
bodies. Inheritance ought to supply them and does not: a program whose only file
object is an `SplTempFileObject` gets a NULL vtable slot for every method the
subclass does not declare, and `$t->ftell()` jumps to address zero — `lldb` stops at
`frame #0: 0x0000000000000000`, and the emitted assembly carries no
`_eir_SplFileObject__ftell` at all. Constructing an `SplFileObject` ANYWHERE in the
same program makes it disappear, which is the signature of a body that was never
emitted rather than a dispatch that went wrong. That gap is left open and named.

SEEK_CUR counted from the wrong place. A buffered read leaves the descriptor ahead
by whatever it kept, and the kernel's SEEK_CUR starts from there — MEASURED on
`"ab\ncd"`: `rewind(); fread($h, 2); fseek($h, 1, SEEK_CUR); ftell($h)` answers 3 in
php and answered 6 here, past the end of a five-byte file. `ftell()` already
subtracted the held bytes; the seek does now too.

FIFTEEN test expectations across the smoke suite were pinning behaviour elephc has
since surpassed — every one re-measured against `php -n` 8.5.6 rather than adjusted
to match. They fell into three families: a warning php raises that the expectation
predates (`Undefined array key`, `Undefined variable`, `Lstat failed for`,
`stat failed for`, `Constant already defined`, the `$escape` deprecations); the
uncaught report and warnings asserted on STDERR when php writes them to STDOUT; and
the trailing element php yields for a file whose last byte is a newline. The suite
goes from 17 failures to 2.

The two that remain fail for REAL reasons and are left alone: `echo` on an
`iterable`-typed parameter raises no `Array to string conversion` where php raises
one per call, and `preg_match($p, $s, $matches)` still cannot write its by-ref
argument.

Verified: 1535 unit, 275 `spl::`, 1097 `io::` tests, the 183-program round-8 corpus
unchanged at 180 identical, and a 46-program streams sweep at 43 identical.

Known residual, isolated to one line of one probe: `feof()` on a `php://temp` stream
is FALSE right after a read consumes the last byte, where php answers true —
`php://memory` and a plain file agree with php. That is what makes an
`SplTempFileObject` iterate one element further than php's.
MSG
git log --oneline -1: 626c9e359 fix(spl): SplTempFileObject was a hand-rolled buffer, and it disagreed with php five ways
